correctness.summary: Endpoint analysis of the square-root density gives the sharp Hellinger constants under the stated half-integral convention, with a Fisher-information transition at kappa=1. Regular variation of endpoint quantiles yields the dyadic asymptotics and universal ratio. An exact geometric sum and exact Laplace Hellinger affinity establish the lattice-phase interval.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: The classical critical linear-boundary rate and nonregular Hellinger methodology are prior art and are not claimed. Searches found no prior explicit critical power-log kappa trichotomy, no sharp asymptotic constants for the Wang--Gao dyadic functional on this endpoint family, and no exact Laplace phase interval for that newly introduced functional. Older nonregular-location literature remains a residual risk for the slowly varying Hellinger refinement alone.

value.summary: The result fills the missing critical endpoint of a recent power-log example, reveals a second logarithmic phase transition, sharpens a new Hellinger--quantile relation on the infinite-information side, and identifies an exact regular-model obstruction to a single fixed-grid asymptotic efficiency constant.

limitations: The critical power-log asymptotics are local as the shift tends to zero.
No remainder uniform in kappa is proved.
The finite-Fisher phase profile is not claimed nonconstant for every compact-support member; exact nonconstancy is shown for Laplace.
The phase-averaging identity is structural and has no estimator or optimality theorem attached.
Cross-model review has not been performed.
review_statement: Same-model review: passed. Cross-model review: not yet performed.
